summary: Credential shadowing across cloud federation causing intermittent KMS decrypt failures for infra ops automation
description: During routine cross-cloud maintenance and scheduled infra tasks, various infra automation jobs intermittently fail with KMS DecryptPermissionDenied. Early signs point to the jobs inheriting stale or shadowed credentials from an ops bastion/pipeline that is federating between AWS and GCP. This ticket tracks investigation and remediation for credential shadowing between AWS->GCP impersonation flows and GKE node workload identity bindings.
impact: Several infra automation jobs (backup encryption key rotation, scheduled snapshot export, and a small subset of Dedicated cluster self-heal tasks) fail intermittently in prod and cause follow-up manual intervention. No customer-facing API outages observed, but operational overhead has increased and there is risk of missed scheduled maintenance affecting SLA adherence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From ops bastion (aws-assumed role) initiate a gcloud auth impersonate flow to target a GCP service account used by backup-scheduler.
2) Run the scheduled snapshot export job against a project that uses KMS key 'proj-prod-rot-01'.
3) Observe DecryptPermissionDenied in the job logs ~20-40% of runs when run shortly after a prior cross-cloud session on the same bastion host.
4) Re-run the job after restarting the bastion agent or clearing cached credentials and the job succeeds consistently.
5) Reproduce more reliably by concurrently running multiple impersonation chains (aws->gcp) and short-lived gcloud auth sessions.

investigation_notes: 03/10 09:12 - Initial triage by infra-oncall (Omar): pattern correlates with short-lived bastion sessions where multiple cross-cloud impersonations happen in rapid succession.

03/10 10:04 - Observed that the gcloud impersonation plugin (v0.7.1) caches access tokens in /var/lib/bastion/.config/gcloud/token_cache and does not always refresh when a different AWS->GCP flow is initiated.

03/10 11:20 - Checked workload identity binding on affected GKE nodepool: backup-runner SA bound correctly. When failure occurs, token presented is from a different GCP SA with no KMS decrypt permissions.

03/10 14:48 - Hypothesis: credential cache + simultaneous cross-cloud binds lead to token mismatch (shadowing). A race in the local auth helper returns the wrong access token to the process invoking KMS.
03/11 08:33 - Reproduced locally by running two impersonations back-to-back on the same bastion user account; confirmed token returned for job belonged to prior impersonation in ~30% runs.
03/11 13:55 - Correlated bastion auth-agent version and linux PAM session multiplexing (systemd user lingering) as possible amplifiers.
03/12 09:10 - SRE prepared a small patch to the bastion auth wrapper that isolates token cache per invocation; queued PR #repo/infra/auth-helper/pull/452 for review.
03/12 11:45 - Short-term mitigation: set env var CLOUDSDK_AUTH_CREDENTIAL_FILE_OVERRIDE per-job to force isolated token files; applied to backup-scheduler and snapshot-export job configs in prod.
root_cause_hypothesis: A shared token cache used by the gcloud impersonation helper on bastion hosts can return a stale token from a prior AWS->GCP impersonation. When processes reuse the same user account and token cache directory, the wrong GCP SA token can be supplied to a task, causing KMS permission errors.
mitigation_workaround: 1) Configure scheduled jobs to set CLOUDSDK_AUTH_CREDENTIAL_FILE_OVERRIDE to a unique path per run to avoid shared token cache collisions. 2) Add a pre-step that calls 'gcloud auth revoke --all' in the job container before any impersonation. 3) Temporarily pin bastion auth-helper to non-multiplexing config and restart the agent on the 3 busiest bastions.
action_items: A1 - Review and merge auth-helper PR #452 to isolate token cache per invocation (owner: infra, assignee: Omar).
A2 - Rollout updated bastion package to prod bastions (canary one host then full) (owner: infra-ops).
A3 - Update backup-scheduler and snapshot-export job templates to set CLOUDSDK_AUTH_CREDENTIAL_FILE_OVERRIDE and include pre-step revoke (owner: platform-team).
A4 - Add monitoring alert for 'KMS DecryptPermissionDenied' spikes and correlate with bastion session churn (owner: observability).
A5 - Postmortem draft and runbook update to include credential-caching pitfalls for cross-cloud ops (owner: security-compliance).
A6 - Longer-term: evaluate switching to short-lived workload identity tokens issued via a central broker that enforces per-process token isolation (owner: architecture).
